findings.title: Float-based child layout breaks after parent becomes a flex container
findings.body: .small-action is turned into a flex container (@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);) but its direct children .topic-avatar (line 270, float: left) and button (line 309, float: right) still rely on float for positioning. Per the CSS Flexbox spec, float has no effect on flex items (it is computed as none), so these declarations become dead code. In particular the action/dismiss button, which previously relied on float: right to sit at the far right of the row, now has no mechanism (no margin-left:auto, order, or justify-content) to stay right-aligned and will simply follow normal flex document order next to the description text. This is a visible layout regression, not merely a performance optimization.

findings.title: Avatar offset padding replaced with percentage value that is inconsistent across widths
findings.body: .small-action-desc previously used padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em (plus margin-top: 5px) to reserve a fixed left offset matching the floated 45px-wide .topic-avatar icon. It was changed to padding: 0 1.5% with the margin-top and the > p padding-top also removed. Since 1.5% is relative to the container width, the gap between the avatar icon and the description text will shrink or grow depending on viewport/container width instead of staying proportional to the fixed-size icon, and the removed vertical offsets likely alter text alignment versus the icon. No corresponding flex-basis/width was added to .topic-avatar to make this proportional spacing correct.

findings.title: Removed bullet badge vertical-alignment fix without replacement
findings.body: The previous rule `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` inside `.extra-info-wrapper` provided a specific vertical offset so bullet-style category badges aligned correctly with surrounding content. This sub-rule was deleted and replaced only with a generic `line-height: 1.5` on the parent, with no compensating offset for `.bullet` badges specifically. This risks a visual misalignment regression for topics that render bullet-style category badges inside `.extra-info-wrapper` (e.g. suggested topics list), and the PR provides no justification for dropping this targeted fix.

findings.title: order() mixin added without establishing a flex parent
findings.body: `@include order(2);` is added to `.extra-info-wrapper`, but the `order` property only has an effect when the element's parent has `display: flex`. Nothing in this file (or the diff) sets `#topic-title` or any ancestor of `.extra-info-wrapper` to `display: flex`. If the parent isn't a flex container (and none is introduced here), this declaration is dead code that gives a false impression the ordering is being controlled, while the actual rendering order is unaffected.

findings.title: Right-alignment of .panel now depends on unverified DOM nesting under the new flex container
findings.body: `.panel` previously used `float: right;` to self-position within `.d-header`. It was changed to `margin-left: auto;` plus `@include order(3);`, which only right-aligns the element if `.panel` is a direct flex-item child of `.contents` (the element that now has `display: flex`). Likewise `.title { float: left; }` was removed entirely. If the actual template markup does not make `.title` and `.panel` direct children of `.contents` (e.g. if there is an intermediate wrapper), both the left title and the right-aligned panel will lose their positioning entirely, since no float fallback remains. The PR does not demonstrate (via markup reference, screenshot, or test) that this structural assumption holds.

findings.title: Non-existent vendor-prefixed property in align-items mixin
findings.body: The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` (line 121). This is not a property that Internet Explorer or any browser ever implemented (the correct and already-present IE10 flexbox alignment prefix is `-ms-flex-align`, on the preceding line). The `-ms-align-items` declaration is dead/invalid CSS that will be silently ignored by all browsers, adding no value and indicating the mixin wasn't verified against actual vendor-prefix requirements.
